Vindicate

/VIN-di-kayt/ - the stress falls on VIN · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Vindicate means to clear someone from blame or show them to have been right, as later events or outside proof do.

The navigator's unfashionable detour around the shoals cost a day and drew jeers, but the wreck of a faster packet on those same rocks vindicated her course within the week.

Worked Example

For twenty years the museum labeled the little portrait 'workshop copy,' overruling the assistant curator who had catalogued it as genuine; the restorer's discovery of the master's signature under the varnish vindicated her at last.

Vindicate does double duty: it clears a person of blame, and it proves a doubted judgment right. That second sense is its signature — evidence can exculpate you of a crime, but only being proved correct can vindicate your decision.

How Vindicate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

justify

justify: shows an action was reasonable; vindicate waits for events to prove it

uphold

uphold: backs a decision on review — without the drama of doubters proved wrong

Antonyms

discredit

discredit: to destroy confidence in a person or claim

disprove

disprove: to show the claim itself was false

How Strong Is It? — support → confirm → vindicate

support vs. vindicate

support vs. vindicate: Evidence may support a theory while the doubters still sneer; support stops far short of vindicate, which settles the argument in its author's favor.

confirm vs. vindicate

confirm vs. vindicate: To confirm a claim is to show it true; confirm stops short of vindicate, which also redeems the person who was mocked for making it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vindic

Root — vindic: to claim, to defend, to avenge

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do

Put it together

Put it together: Vindic- (from Latin vindicare, 'to claim, to defend, to avenge') + -ate = to stand up for successfully. Latin vindex was the champion who stepped in to defend another's cause; vengeance took the root down its harsher road, while vindicate kept the courtroom sense — a name or a judgment defended and won back.

Use the root in a new word: vengeance

Use the root in a new word: vengeance: The old ballads run on vengeance — a wrong answered in kind, blow for blow.

Word Choice

formal / journalistic

Vindicate is the headline word for doubters proved wrong. In this unit's clearing family, evidence exculpates, boards exonerate, authorities absolve — vindicate is what time and events do, and alone among them it can take your judgment, your gamble, or your theory as its object, not just you.
